strongest_angle: Examine how eastern and southern Australian Bogong moths soar across 600 miles (1,000 km) to aestivate in the Australian Alps using both stellar cues and Earth's geomagnetic field.

key_facts.fact: Bogong moths migrate biannually up to 1,000 kilometers between their breeding areas in eastern and southern Australia and aestivation sites in the Australian Alps.
Each spring, billions of Bogong moths emerge from the soil across southeast Australia, including south-eastern Queensland and far-western Victoria, traveling to cool caves.
Bogong moths navigate using a stellar compass at night as well as a light-dependent geomagnetic inclination compass to reach ancestral summer caves.
National Geographic writer Elizabeth Landau reported that a new generation of gray-and-brown Bogong moths soars some 600 miles to converge on crevices and caves in the Australian Alps.
